messages.content:
The issue occurs in the `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class. This method is responsible for printing the help message for the command-line.

The failing test case `testInfiniteLoop` creates an `Options` object, adds an option with a long description, sets the width of the help formatter to 20, and then calls `formatter.printHelp("app", options)`. This triggers the `printHelp` method with the provided arguments.

The current bug report describes that when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes with an `OutOfMemoryError`. The failing test case triggers this behavior by setting the width of the help formatter to 20, which is not enough to display the long description on a single line, causing the infinite loop.

To fix this issue, the width of the help formatter needs to be set to a value that can accommodate the length of the description without causing an infinite loop. Increasing the width or implementing a mechanism to handle long descriptions that do not fit in a single line would prevent the infinite loop and the eventual crash.

Next, let's identify the best locations to fix this issue.
